title: From Border Town to 18 Million People #shorts
description:
In 1979 Shenzhen had about 300,000 people. Then it became China's first Special Economic Zone.

New China Short every day; full reality-show recap every Saturday. Subscribe to @mainlandunpacked.

Sources: Investment Monitor; The Plan; Shenzhen Statistics Bureau. Footage: Phuketian Mobi (CC BY).

scenes.text: In 1979, this city had about 300,000 people.
headline: BORDER TOWN
TO MEGACITY

scenes.text: In 1980, Shenzhen became China's first Special Economic Zone, a test lab for markets and foreign money.

events.text: Small town on the Hong Kong border

scenes.text: Today, almost 18 million people live here.
scenes.label: up from about 0.3 million in 1979

scenes.text: Its economy grew more than 20% a year on average, for four decades.
scenes.label: average growth, 1979 to 2019
scenes.image: File:Shenzhen Skyline Fuhua Road Ping An International Finance Center.jpg

scenes.text: Huawei, Tencent, BYD and DJI are all headquartered here.
Should other countries copy the Shenzhen playbook?
scenes.question: SHOULD OTHERS COPY IT?
